item.title: Britain renames East Jerusalem to 'U.K. Mission, Jerusalem' consulate after Israel announces closure
item.description: Britain denied the closure of its East Jerusalem consulate, saying it will remain operational under a new name after Israel said the mission had 'ended its operations' over U.K. sanctions targeting Israeli settlements
item.dc:creator: Liza Rozovsky

item.title: Five arrested in London after pro-Palestinian protest on October 7 anniversary
item.description: Police said the five, detained outside the U.K. Jewish community's representative body, chanted slogans calling for 'intifada.' They remained in custody over alleged incitement to racial hatred, amid restrictions on a march and counter-protests
item.dc:creator: Ben Kroll

item.title: Israel's European allies and critics mark October 7, acknowledge antisemitism
item.description: From pro-Netanyahu allies across Europe to politicians calling to recognize Palestinian suffering during the three years of war, leaders worldwide marked the third anniversary of Hamas' attack, as some leaders remained silent on social media
item.dc:creator: Ben Kroll

item.title: Israeli, EU officials condemn politician over taking down of Israeli flag at October 7 tribute
item.description: Rima Hassan acknowledged removing an Israeli flag from an October 7 memorial at the European Parliament, saying the EU flag fell as a result. Her office said the action was meant to protest Israel's 'ongoing genocide' in Gaza, not the victims' memory
item.dc:creator: Liza Rozovsky

item.title: U.K. Green Party leader vows to protect Jews after 'Zionism is racism' vote
item.description: Polanski said criticism of Israel and antisemitism must remain distinct after members voted to define Zionism as racism, while deputy Rachel Millward opposed the motion. Israel said it would ban him from entering the country over the vote
item.dc:creator: Ben Kroll

item.title: Germany arrests ex-chief spy on espionage and treason charges
item.description: German media said the foreign intelligence service that used August Hanning was not Russian. Evidence reportedly emerged during a probe into the abduction of an heiress's children in Denmark involving former Israeli agents
item.dc:creator: DPA

item.title: Man who planned terror attack on London's Israeli embassy jailed for at least 20 years
item.description: Abdullah Albadri, 34, attempted to breach the Israeli Embassy's perimeter in west London in April 2025 before being stopped by armed police. Prosecutors said he intended to attack the embassy in revenge for Israel's actions in Gaza
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Australia probes possible radicalization of co-pilot in flydubai flight to Israel
item.description: Australian public broadcaster ABC reported that a probe is being conducted by a multi-agency effort to determine whether the pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, was radicalized while studying in the country between 2015 and 2017
item.dc:creator: Ben Kroll

item.title: Ireland's head soccer coach asks to prevent future matches against Israel
item.description: After two politically charged matches, Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrímsson urged UEFA to keep the teams apart, citing strong Irish support for Palestine and saying he 'would not wish' another country to endure a similar two weeks against Israel
item.dc:creator: Ben Kroll

item.title: Spain's prime minister calls snap election as left-wing government faces ouster
item.description: The election is scheduled for November 29. An election defeat would spell the end of one of Europe's last few left-leaning governments at a time when the far-right is making unprecedented gains across the region
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Brazil to hold runoff as Netanyahu ally Bolsonaro leads Lula in presidential vote
item.description: The two candidates hold opposing views on Israel, with Lula calling Israel's war a 'genocide.' Bolsonaro vowed to move Brazil's embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem within the first six months of his mandate
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Israel bans U.K. Green Party leader Zack Polanski after 'Zionism is racism' vote
item.description: Polanski, who is Jewish, did not vote on the motion defining Zionism as a 'racist ideology' and has backed amendments to soften its wording. Britain's ruling Labour Party condemned it, saying, 'It is shameful to vote against a two-state solution'
item.dc:creator: Haaretz

item.title: U.K. Green Party votes against Israel as Jewish state: 'Zionism is racism'
item.description: The Green Party voted to adopt a motion defining Zionism as a 'racist ideology,' with 1,022 party members voting in favor and 813 who voted against. Party leaders and Jewish members warned it risks alienating Jewish supporters and fueling division
item.dc:creator: Daniella Peled

item.title: U.K. Green Party conference debates controversial 'Zionism is racism' motion
item.description: Party leaders and Jewish members warn the proposal risks alienating Jewish supporters and fueling division, while some activists push to reject leadership-backed amendments intended to soften the motion's language and implications
item.dc:creator: Haaretz

item.title: Germany bracing for 'serious' hybrid attacks by Russia, Chancellor Merz says
item.description: Merz said Germany would respond 'quickly and clearly,' while Russian ‌President Vladimir Putin warned that harsh retaliation can lead to 'a fatal point of no return'
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: U.K. Prime Minister Burnham says 'strong indications' Iran involved in suspected plan to target U.S. air base
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made these remarks after the five suspects involved in the Fairford air base incident were released on bail, and after the U.S. secretary of state also pointed at 'a foreign actor'
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Israeli diaspora minister backs French far-right leader amid antisemitism allegations
item.description: After the publication of antisemitic messages Jordan Bardella wrote as a teenager, Israeli Diaspora Minister Amichai Chikli came out in defense of the National Rally leader, accusing the French left of 'character assassination, like Israeli leftists'
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: U2's Bono compares Ben-Gvir to Nazi Himmler over Gaza rhetoric
item.description: Bono condemned Hamas' October 7 attack But he said he was particularly horrified by Ben-Gvir's statements about Palestinians in Gaza. The band recently released an EP dedicated to people killed in conflicts around the world
item.dc:creator: Haaretz

item.title: French far-right leader and Israel ally denies past antisemitic remarks
item.description: Jordan Bardella sued a French outlet over claims he wrote that 'all the banks are owned by Jews' over a decade ago. The National Rally leader has cultivated close ties with the Netanyahu government while seeking to shed his party's racist image
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: U.K. police release on bail terror suspects arrested at airbase used for Iran strikes
item.description: A source familiar with the investigation said an Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely, as the British government, has given authorization to the U.S. to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Europe's boycott of Israel is rapidly expanding – and it won't be easy to stop
item.description: From Dutch supermarkets removing settlement products to the Irish push to boycott their Israel match, calls for economic and cultural boycotts are intensifying across Europe – reflecting growing frustration on the continent with Israel's conduct
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Lis

item.title: Israel's embrace is a gift to Austria's far right, but it comes with hidden risks
item.description: Israel's government is helping Austria's Freedom Party ward off accusations of antisemitism, but in the eyes of its own supporters, the embrace could make the party look like part of the system it claims to despise
item.dc:creator: Liam Hoare

item.title: Trump says men arrested at U.K. air base used by U.S. were looking to do 'big damage'
item.description: Five men were arrested near RAF Fairford on suspicion of terrorism offenses. An Iranian-linked motive is considered most likely, while Russian and Islamist plots are also being investigated
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Report: Ex-Hamas chief's bodyguard planned attacks on Jews in Europe while seeking asylum in U.K.
item.description: According to The Times, the bodyguard received British citizenship about a decade ago, even though his ties to the Hamas were known. The attacks were scheduled for the second anniversary of October 7, but were foiled before they were carried out
item.dc:creator: Haaretz

item.title: East German town backs AfD motion to halt new Holocaust memorial plaques
item.description: The decision in Heidenau, a town near Dresden in the eastern state of Saxony, comes as the AfD tops national polls ahead of Chancellor Merz's centre-right Christian Democratic Union
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: 150 Berlin Jews, Israelis back Left-led government, rejecting Israel's antisemitism claim
item.description: Prominent Jewish cultural figures and Israelis in Berlin signed an open letter welcoming Die Linke's victory. Israel's embassy in Berlin criticized the letter, saying its signatories 'speak no more for Jews in Germany than any other group'
item.dc:creator: Haaretz

item.title: Colombia withdraws from Gaza genocide case against Israel at International Court of Justice
item.description: While no official reason was given for the withdrawal, it's the latest in a series of pro-Israel decisions made by the new, right-wing government in Bogota
item.dc:creator: Ben Kroll

item.title: Does Germany's Die Linke have an antisemitism problem – and could it keep the party from power in Berlin?
item.description: Potential coalition partners are demanding that the far-left party confront antisemitism in its ranks. But party leaders and experts say isolated incidents are being politicized to derail a left-led government
item.dc:creator: Vera Weidenbach

item.title: In a Changing World, Switzerland Votes on the Meaning of Neutrality
item.description: As Switzerland prepares to vote on the 'Neutrality Initiative,' citizens must decide what neutrality actually means
item.dc:creator: Netta Ahituv

item.title: Berlin Jews face 'immediate existential threat' after far-left party wins election, Israeli envoy says
item.description: Ambassador Ron Prosor accused Die Linke, a far-left party, of 'deep-rooted' antisemitism after its Berlin election victory; party leader Elif Eralp has rejected the allegations and vowed to protect Jewish life
item.dc:creator: DPA

item.title: Far-right AfD party leads Germany state election, as Merz party suffers major defeat
item.description: AfD gained ground in elections in both Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, but the far-right party is still unable to form a regional government. Sunday's election was Merz's CDU party's worst regional election defeat in postwar ​Germany
item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Likud minister Miri Regev speaks at confab hosted by Nazi-linked Austrian FPO party
item.description: The conference was organized by Freedom Party lawmaker Harald Vilimsky, dedicated to 'the threats facing Europe from antisemitism and Islamist movements.' The party was led by former Nazis in the postwar period
item.dc:creator: Liza Rozovsky

item.title: Swedish election left the blocs closer on policy – but split over Israel and antisemitism
item.description: The center-left won Sweden's election by a slim margin, but now comes the hard part
item.dc:creator: David Stavrou

item.title: The Ceuta crisis exposed Europe's schism on asylum. The hard-liners are winning
item.description: Europe is split between the Danish and Spanish approaches to asylum: a fortress Europe curbing migration and a more open Continent attuned to its labor needs and the integration of migrants over the long term
item.dc:creator: Liam Hoare

item.title: Germany charges suspected Hamas members over plot to target Jews on Oct. 7 anniversary
item.description: According to the indictment, Hamas had been planning a specific assassination attack in Germany or Austria against Israeli representatives, Jews or pro-Israel individuals since at least July 2025
item.dc:creator: DPA
